properties.title: Flood Advisory issued October 28 at 6:25AM HST until October 28 at 9:30AM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...The island of Molokai in Maui County...

* WHEN...Until 930 AM HST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding on roads, poor drainage areas, and in
streams. Overflowing poor drainage areas. River or stream flows are
elevated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 622 AM HST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
rainfall rates diminishing over Molokai. However, a rapid rise
was noted at Kawela Gulch, so the flood advisory will be
extended. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly
in the advisory area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
the entire island of Molokai.
properties.instruction:
Rainfall and runoff will also cause hazardous driving conditions due
to ponding, reduced visibility and poor braking action.

A Flood Watch is also in effect for Maui County through tonight.

properties.title: Marine Weather Statement issued October 28 at 10:59AM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
The areas affected include...
Caribbean waters of Puerto Rico from 10 NM to 17N, including the
coastal waters of Saint Croix...
Coastal Waters of Southern Puerto Rico out 10 NM...

* At 1059 AM AST, Doppler radar indicated a line of strong showers
and isolated thunderstorms, capable of producing winds to around 30
knots. These strong thunderstorms were located just offshore of
Salinas/Guayama along a north to southwest line to 17 NM over
Caribbean waters of Puerto Rico.

This strong thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.
properties.instruction:
Report severe weather to the Coast Guard or nearest law enforcement
agency. They will relay your report to the National Weather Service
office.

Mariners can expect gusty winds to around 30 knots, locally higher
waves, some lightning strikes, and heavy downpours. Boaters should
seek safe harbor immediately until these storms pass.
properties.area: Caribbean Waters of Puerto Rico from 10 NM to 17N, including the Coastal Waters of Saint Croix; Coastal Waters of Southern Puerto Rico out 10 NM

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 28 at 9:03AM EDT until October 29 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Florida...

St Johns River Near Deland affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Upstream persistent gusty northeast winds and tidal effects on the
St John River are slowing flow. At Deland, the river is forecast to
crest near Minor Flood Stage the next couple days, then begin a slow
decline through Action Stage later in the week.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Docks and piers are completely submerged at
Pier 44 Marina. Many docks are partially submerged at Hontoon
Landing Marina.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EDT Wednesday the stage was 4.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 4.0 feet
the next couple days. It will then fall below flood stage late in
the week.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 1215 AM EDT.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 28 at 8:58AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Persistent gusty northeast winds and upstream tidal effects are
slowing river flow on the St Johns River at Astor. River levels are
forecast to begin a slow decline late this week, but remain in
Moderate Flood stage for at least the next couple weeks.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland, Astor...Moderate flooding
is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Major flooding occurs with water entering
many structures on canals and along the river. Long duration
flooding will occur, with levels taking weeks to months to return
below flood stage. Water rescues will be necessary. River Road
becomes inaccessible, with 1 to 2 feet water depth in numerous
homes on Wildhog, Possum, Bonnet and Snail roads. Roads along Blue
Creek are inaccessible with major flooding of homes on Otter,
Branch and Chestnut roads. Camp South Moon Road and Juno Trail are
inaccessible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EDT Wednesday the stage was 3.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EDT Wednesday was 3.8 feet.
- Forecast...River levels are forecast to crest around 3.8 feet
this week, then begin a gradual decline late in the week.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 200 AM EDT.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued October 27 at 7:44PM MDT until October 30 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a Flood
Advisory for the following rivers in New Mexico...

Rio Grande at Embudo affecting Rio Arriba and Taos Counties.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Rio Grande at Embudo.

* WHEN...From this evening to Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 8.0 feet, Minor overbank flows are occurring above the
Embudo gaging site. Access to riverside picnic facilities above
Pilar and below the Taos Junction Bridge along State Route 570 will
be limited if further rises occur. Water may be extremely close to
underside of bridge over Rio Grande on Aguas Caliente Rd in Pilar.
Other localized effects due to the high water levels will begin to
be felt at a stage of 10 feet but no significant flooding is
expected until the river rises to 12 feet.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:00 PM MDT Tuesday the stage was 7.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 8.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 8.4 feet
early Thursday morning.
- Action stage is 8.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 10.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
If you encounter a flooded roadway, turn around and find an
alternative route.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued Wednesday afternoon at noon MDT.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 27 at 6:50PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in New
Mexico...

Rio Chama Below Chamita affecting Rio Arriba County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Chama below Chamita.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 6.0 feet, properties in the flood plain along the Rio
Chama and near the junction of the Rio Ojo Caliente will see water
in their yards. Impacts can include bank erosion and damage to
wells and septic tanks.  These impacts will increase in severity at
higher river levels.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:00 PM MDT Tuesday the stage was 6.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 5.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 6:00 PM MDT Tuesday was 6.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to oscillate around 6.4 to 6.5
feet through Wednesday.
- Flood stage is 6.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 6.4
feet on 07/21/2009.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued Wednesday afternoon at noon MDT.
